statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is 4, low, because CME equity index futures have been halted since Friday at 21:00Z and fourteen of the twenty-four hours published here contain no tradable interval at all; only the ten slots from the scheduled 22:00Z Sunday reopen onward are tradable, and they carry conditional Tail readings of 12, 13, 12, 11, 10, 10, 10, 10, 11 and 12 that all stay far below the block threshold. Stress is 34, moderate: the 50% US tariff on about $20 billion of Canadian goods is in force after trade talks collapsed, Canada has dated a dollar-for-dollar match to 8 September, a Monday US Treasury press conference on isolating Iran's economy is scheduled, the thirty-year Treasury yield sits at 5.23% on the latest H.15 daily column, and crude has gained about 5% for a second consecutive week, none of it able to reach price until the venue reopens. Confidence is 86, high: index level, yields, volatility, energy, the seven-day calendar and the weekend news set were each re-verified against primary sources this hour, and the only missing input is live price-path evidence, which no source can supply while the market is shut.
recommendation: The last observed session remains consistent with functioning mean reversion rather than a one-way path: cash NDX opened at 29,359.60, traded down to 29,142.44, recovered to 29,405.12 and closed at 29,308.86, up 0.33% on the day and below its own open, ending a five-day losing streak, while the VIX settled at 14.89, down 6.0% and near the low of a 14.77-15.95 range. Both session extremes were retraced and neither produced repeated extension after a failed pullback, so no Tail amplifier carries over from observed structure. Friday internals were split rather than aligned, with application and infrastructure software up about 1.2% against semiconductors down 0.31%, megacap dispersion was wide at roughly 1.8 points, and cross-asset direction was mixed, with gold higher, energy higher and Treasury futures lower. The Nasdaq 100 still finished the week down about 0.90% while the Dow set a record close. Mapped policy state remains EA_ON across the whole horizon. The narrow evidence-based danger window covers 22:00Z to 02:00Z, the reopen gap and the thin hours before Asian cash liquidity is fully engaged, and it rests on a conditional scenario rather than on observed structure.
headline: Closed-venue assessment with ten reopen hours inside the horizon: Tail holds the floor of 4 through fourteen shut hours, then carries conditional readings of 12, 13, 12, 11, 10, 10, 10, 10, 11 and 12 from the 22:00Z Sunday reopen, while live US tariffs on Canadian goods, a scheduled Monday Treasury announcement on isolating Iran, a post-2007 long end and a second week of energy gains stay unpriced.
body:
CME Globex equity index futures stopped trading for the week on Friday at 21:00Z and are scheduled to reopen on Sunday at 22:00Z. The twenty-four slots published here run from 2026-08-23T08:00:00Z to 2026-08-24T07:00:00Z, so the reopen slot and the first nine hours after it sit inside the horizon while the first fourteen do not. Cash NDX settled at 29,308.86 on Friday, up 0.33% from a 29,213.17 prior close, after opening at 29,359.60 and printing a 29,142.44 low and a 29,405.12 high; both extremes were retraced inside the session, the close finished below the open, and the day ended a five-day losing streak even as the index still lost about 0.90% on the week. That is a two-sided path, and it is the last observable Nasdaq-100 structure in existence, so nothing in the current evidence set supports a persistent no-retracement regime. Tail therefore holds its closed-venue floor of 4 for every shut hour.

The information set that will meet the reopen is unusually dense and entirely unpriced. Trade talks between Washington and Ottawa collapsed minutes before a midnight deadline, a 50% US tariff on roughly $20 billion of Canadian exports took effect, and Prime Minister Carney has dated a dollar-for-dollar Canadian response to 8 September. The US Treasury has scheduled a Monday press conference to detail the plan to isolate Iran's economy, and over the weekend Iranian officials restated that Tehran will not submit, with a senior security official threatening wider Strait of Hormuz disruption if neighbouring states join the campaign; Hormuz flows are already running near 8-9 million barrels per day. WTI sits near $87.06 and Brent near $94.39 after a second consecutive week of roughly 5% gains. The latest H.15 daily column shows the 30-year Treasury at 5.23%, the 10-year at 4.69% and the 2-year at 4.19%, with the long end at its highest since 2007 and the main drag on technology through the prior week.

Cross-asset and internal evidence is split rather than aligned, which is why this stack raises Stress and not Tail. Latest-session megacaps were five up and three down with dispersion near 1.8 points, semiconductors averaged -0.70% against software gains above 1.1%, gold rose about 2.4%, crude was firm and Treasury futures were lower across the curve. That pattern describes hedging and rotation, not a single directional impulse capable of denying mean reversion. Shared delayed cross-asset context was used only as confirmation; it is not live Nasdaq-100 price-path evidence and was not used to set the current action.

Stress is published at 34 for the current hour and rises through the shut session to 46 by the last closed slot, crossing into the elevated band as the reopen concentrates all weekend repricing into a single auction. From the 22:00Z reopen the ten tradable slots carry conditional Tail of 12 and a horizon peak of 13 in the first full hour, easing to 12 as Tokyo opens, 11 as Hong Kong and mainland liquidity join, and a floor of 10 through the quiet Asian hours, before edging back to 11 at the European pre-open and 12 at the European cash open, where the first cross-venue repricing of the new week lands. Every one of those readings is a conditional scenario derived from gap and liquidity mechanics, not an observation, and every one maps to green.

The named invalidation is specific: a reopen gap that is defended rather than retraced, with shallow pullbacks and repeated extension after failed retracements, and with yields, energy, semiconductors and breadth turning aligned behind it. That structure would raise Tail at the next hourly assessment. Its absence, together with an orderly retrace and decaying volatility, would confirm the published path. Beyond this horizon the week's checkpoints are Wednesday's July PCE and second-estimate GDP with Nvidia results after the close, and Friday's Jackson Hole keynote alongside the preliminary payrolls benchmark revision, all carried as scheduled items in the events calendar; the Monday Treasury press conference on Iran is a further checkpoint whose exact time is not published, so it is described in the hourly drivers rather than dated in the calendar. None of these has occurred and none is treated here as observed.

The following thirteen slots describe the same closed market, so Tail holds 4 and the mapped policy state stays EA_ON throughout them, while Stress holds 34 through the quiet Sunday European hours and then rebuilds to 46 by the last shut hour as the reopen approaches with the information set unchanged. The final ten slots are tradable: the 22:00Z scheduled reopen carries a conditional Tail of 12, the first full hour after it the horizon peak of 13, the hour containing the Tokyo cash open a conditional 12, then 11 as Hong Kong and mainland liquidity join and a floor of 10 through the quiet Asian hours, before 11 at the European pre-open and 12 at the European cash open. All of those readings rest on gap and thin-liquidity scenarios rather than on observed structure, and all remain green. The invalidation to watch in the first tradable hours is a reopen gap that is defended rather than retraced, with repeated extension after failed pullbacks; that structure would raise Tail at the next hourly assessment, and its absence would confirm the published path.
